audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Yorick wins 54.97% over 3140 games and the chart gave him zero of seven stages. Three rows also contradicted their own prose — level 3 read Jayce while whys[2] says ghouls even the wave, levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] says he chunks you, level 6 read Jayce while whys[4] says it stays skill-based, and first item read Skill while whys[5] gives it to him.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row. Aligning them to the prose reproduces the packet chart exactly, except for the last row — and a champion who wins 55% has to own something.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 and 4 to Skill at 5/10, rows 3 and 5 to Jayce at 3/10, row 6 to Yorick at 6/10, as matched full/content pairs. Two-plus items is the row the page's own late paragraph and spikes[3] already describe as yours: Maiden and ghouls take towers Jayce cannot defend alone. whys[6] restated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating read 8.5/10 with report[14] calling it 'Hard', against a diff of FAV and a 54.97% win rate.
audit.why: Three signals, two answers, on the same page.
audit.corrected: 5/10 with the two lines that quote the number brought along.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls his knockback 'Melee Q' and describes his R as merely 'no game-changing ult'.
audit.why: The hammer knockback is Thundering Blow (E); the hammer Q is To the Skies!, a leap. And the R is not nothing: it is a 6-second stance swap whose first attack after swapping to Mercury Cannon reduces your armour and magic resist — that swap animation is the burst tell. Separately, To the Skies! is a dash, so Dark Procession's terrain denies his only way into melee.
audit.corrected: Slots named correctly, the armour-and-MR shred on the swap stated with the swap as the tell, and the terrain block on To the Skies! written into spikes[3] and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Every line says 'when Shock Blast is down' with no number.
audit.why: Shock Blast runs 16s at rank 1 down to 6s, which is the difference between a real window and a two-second one.
